title: Large-volume snapshot compaction capacity
resolved_by: TQP-42 sparse hierarchy storage and large-world compaction
observations: The documented 2K volumetric procedural profile contains roughly 299,520 catalog pages across its LOD hierarchy.
The former all-pages native snapshot path rejected this procedural catalog during snapshot-manifest validation before compaction.
The replacement stores the procedural descriptor and a bounded sparse baked/edit overlay instead of materializing every declared page.
The same large world reopens successfully from its procedural source and durable edit journal, preserving committed authoritative samples.

The retained TQP-42 workload compacts central and finite-boundary edits, reopens and migrates the snapshot, reproduces authoritative samples and adaptive resources, and leaves no partial publication on failure.
bounded_conclusion: Large-world sparse procedural snapshot compaction is qualified only for the retained Windows 128x16x128-chunk profile and declared limits.
The result does not qualify arbitrary explicit catalogs, immutable production save compatibility, or unbounded worlds.
No evidence attributes this limit to Transvoxel meshing tables or terrain geometry correctness.

disposition.TQP-27: Retain the historical all-pages capacity rejection as the negative control that motivated TQP-42.
disposition.TQP-42: Close this finding for the retained sparse procedural snapshot profile using exact native, Godot, performance, recovery, migration, and atomic-publication evidence.
disposition.production: Keep generic production save compatibility unqualified until the production-addon and release milestones define and qualify a stable format and wider fault envelope.
